methods: September 3 CSI intake: verified the exact 18-page MiEnviro rendition of MDEQ's June 15, 2018 Cadillac WWTP final compliance sampling inspection report, including all four sparse interior pages and its native-email/workbook provenance.

September 2 VN-019184 intake: both supplied five-page PDFs were hashed, opened, OCR-read and rendered. They are exact duplicate copies of Cadillac's July 14 response despite one misleading notice filename. The distinct June 10 EGLE notice already in the catalog was localized, the response was added once, and the agency notice and municipal response were placed in separate timeline events.

September 2 EPA QNCR intake: all three supplied reports and all 150 pages were opened, text-extracted and rendered. Two exact existing records were localized for anonymous first-page preview and full download, and the distinct 47-page January–March 2015 report was added after a corpus-wide SHA-256 check.
SHA-256 comparison within the category and against every published catalog
Embedded-text extraction from every PDF page
OCR of every image and PDF page with fewer than 40 normalized embedded characters
Manual visual review of low-confidence aerial-image and rotated-table pages

decisions.name: 2018 Cadillac WWTP compliance sampling inspection final report
decisions.reason: The exact 18-page MiEnviro PDF rendition is retained once as the readable compliance record. It includes the June 15 MDEQ transmittal and the report tables from the original workbook. The native MSG and XLSX are preserved in their format-appropriate archives and cross-referenced rather than collapsed into the PDF. Four sparse interior pages are intentional workbook-pagination artifacts, not missing content. No PFAS analytes were reported.

decisions.name: VN-019184 notice and response reconciliation
decisions.reason: The two supplied files have the same 784,458-byte binary and SHA-256 hash and both contain Cadillac's signed July 14, 2026 response, NOAA precipitation table and two EGLE reporting emails. The response is retained once under a content-accurate title. The separate 95,700-byte June 10 EGLE notice already in the catalog was localized and cross-referenced. EGLE's violation findings and Cadillac's RDS assertion remain separate, and no final agency disposition is inferred.

decisions.reason: No byte-identical or page-for-page render-identical duplicates were found among the remaining compliance source records. Similar titles, source extracts, revisions, raw MSG files and rendered email PDFs were retained when their content or format differed.

decisions.reason: The two 65-page PDFs have identical normalized text and identical rendered pixels on all 65 pages. Their byte hashes differ only because the PDF metadata timestamps differ by four seconds. The clean filename was retained and the copy-number filename was suppressed as an actual duplicate.

decisions.name: 2022 CEI report and transmittal package
decisions.reason: Both records were retained. The 24-page transmittal contains the complete 21-page CEI report plus three pages of formal agency correspondence; the added correspondence makes the package a distinct evidentiary record, not an actual duplicate of the standalone report.

decisions.name: August 29 Dropbox mixed-category intake
decisions.reason: Fifty supplied PDFs totaling 1,406 pages were checked by SHA-256, page count, PDF metadata, embedded text and cross-catalog comparison. Forty-seven are byte-for-byte matches to records already preserved in the app. The three unmatched compliance PDFs were then rendered page-by-page, and OCR was applied to the only sparse page; all three passed readability and page-integrity checks.

decisions.name: 2023 standalone inspection form and transmittal package
decisions.reason: Both records were retained. Pages 4 through 19 of the 29-page September 29 transmittal render identically to the complete 16-page July 10 inspection form, but the transmittal also has 13 distinct email, cover and final-sampling-report pages. It is therefore a wrapper package with additional evidence, not an actual duplicate.

decisions.name: 2025 NPDES compliance evaluation inspection report
decisions.reason: The 16-page June 10, 2025 facility site-review report has a distinct SHA-256, normalized-text fingerprint and rendered-page sequence not found in the published corpus. It is retained alongside the already preserved August 19 compliance communication because the report supplies the detailed inspection record while the communication states the formal findings and corrective-action request.

decisions.name: 2026 Cadillac cyanide correspondence sequence
decisions.reason: All 24 image-based pages received OCR and were checked in rendered sequence. The package is distinct from every published compliance record and preserves dated municipal, agency, laboratory and industrial-user messages from February 27 through July 7, 2026. Statements remain attributed to their authors and are not promoted into an independent adjudication.

decisions.name: August 31 POTW monitoring and post-inspection intake
decisions.reason: Ten supplied PDFs totaling 37 pages were checked by SHA-256, page count, embedded text, rendered-page sequence and full visual review. Nine annual monitoring summaries exactly match established IPP records. The distinct four-page November 19, 2009 post-inspection export was retained once in the compliance library and linked to one dated event.
